title: Flame Arrestor

introduction.definition: A flame arrestor is a passive device that lets gas flow but stops a flame propagating through it. Its element divides the flow into many narrow channels; a flame entering them loses heat to the metal so quickly that it cannot sustain combustion and is extinguished.
key_points: Gap selected for the gas explosion group (MESG)
Installation distance limits for in-line types

classification.type: In-line deflagration flame arrestor, crimped-ribbon element

introduction.summary: A flame arrestor lets gas or vapour flow through but stops a flame from passing. Its element divides the flow into many very narrow channels; a flame entering them loses heat to the metal so fast that it is cooled below ignition and extinguished. In-line deflagration arrestors protect tanks, vent headers and burners against flashback.

foundation: Support the valve and adjoining pipe so the body does not carry pipe weight or thermal loads; heavy valves need their own supports.
alignment: Align flanges face-to-face and bore-to-bore before bolting; never pull pipes into place with the bolts.
Respect the flow-direction arrow on the body.
piping: Respect the maximum distance between ignition source and arrestor stated in the certificate.
Provide ΔP monitoring and access for element removal.
commissioning: Check the valve strokes fully and smoothly.
Pressure-test the line (shell test) with the valve partly open; do not use the valve to blind a test above its seat rating.
Record the as-installed position and set points.

causes: Wrong gas group, damaged element, stabilised burning beyond rating

video_tutorials.title: Flame Arrestor — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Flame Arrestor.
A flame arrestor is a passive device that lets gas flow but stops a flame propagating through it.
Its element divides the flow into many narrow channels; a flame entering them loses heat to the metal so quickly that it cannot sustain combustion and is extinguished.
Typical applications include storage tank vents (with PV valves); vapour recovery and vent headers; flare and incinerator lines; gas burner and biogas lines.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Housing (two halves bolted around the element).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Flame Arrestor — Operation

script.narration: How the Flame Arrestor works.
Gas flows through the housing; the housing enlarges so velocity in the element is low.
The crimped-ribbon element creates thousands of narrow triangular channels.
A flame front travelling back towards the element enters the channels.
Heat is drawn into the metal walls; the flame cools below ignition and goes out.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
The element splits the flow into many narrow channels.

video_tutorials.title: Flame Arrestor — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Flame Arrestor.
Check ΔP or flow restriction.
Remove and clean the element.
Replace element after a flame event or damage.
Watch for element fouling/blocking: high δp, tank pressure/vacuum problems. Common cause: polymerising vapours, dust, ice.
Watch for flame transmission: fire downstream. Common cause: wrong gas group, damaged element, stabilised burning beyond rating.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
